look_here_first: Look at the basal leaves first: huge, stiff, deeply pinnatifid blades cut almost to the midrib into narrow lobes. Then check the towering flowering stem and yellow ray-and-disk heads. Leaf north-south orientation is variable and not diagnostic by itself.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Prior B064 review could not confirm three native target-zone counties; Hays/Purola record represents introduced planting, not native range evidence.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Do not count planted compass plants or state-level Texas nativity as target-county native proof.

best_field_traits: Massive deeply pinnatifid basal leaves with narrow lobes.
Very tall erect flowering stalk, often above a basal leaf rosette.
Yellow ray florets and central disk florets in sunflower-like heads.
Stiff coarse foliage; inspect leaf dissection rather than flower color.
Leaves sometimes held approximately north-south, but orientation alone is unreliable.

comparisons.key_distinctions: S. radula has broader rough leaves rather than the extremely deeply dissected compass leaves. S. albiflorum has white rays and different leaf architecture. S. integrifolium has broad mostly entire leaves; historic Central Texas variety names need concept-level reconciliation.
comparisons.warning: Separate cultivated local plants from native county occurrences.
